title: Accelerate first-success for SDKs & Docs with funnel hypotheses
creator: Ravi Shah
description: Objective: Reduce time-to-first-success for new developer signups by improving the SDK + docs + quickstart funnel. We will run a sequence of lightweight experiments that combine micro-copy changes, interactive quickstarts, and an in-console SDK starter that pre-populates API keys and sample code. Hypothesis: increasing 'first-run success' from 22% -> 45% will double 14-day retention and increase API usage by measurable units. This ticket scopes the playbook, success metrics, experimental matrix, and rollout plan for Cycle 2026-W10 through W13.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment matrix (3 variants) defined and prioritized
Instrumentation dashboards for first-success and 14-day retention created and validated
Two quickstart variants implemented and A/B ready in docs + console
Automated cohort tracking for users who complete the quickstart
Runbook for rollforward/rollback and metric thresholds documented

2026-02-18 - Ravi Shah: Consolidated metric definitions in Confluence. First-success defined as a user making a single successful API call that returns generation tokens and completes without 4xx/5xx errors within 5 minutes of onboarding.

2026-02-25 - Elena Morales: Design mockups reviewed — inline code snippets + runnable playground. Design suggested a 'Run in Console' CTA that pre-fills a template for the most common use case: chat generation with streaming. Design flagged accessibility checks.

2026-03-03 - Eng (PR 1042): Instrumentation PR opened to emit events: onboarding.start, onboarding.first_success, onboarding.failure_reason. Requesting review from analytics and infra to ensure event schema and sampling are correct.
2026-03-05 - Analytics (note): Confirmed event schema and created dashboard queries for first_success_rate by cohort and channel. Set up a baseline dashboard with rolling 7-day and 14-day windows.

2026-03-08 - Elena Morales: Experiment matrix approved — Control, inline quickstart (docs), console-run (pre-populated). Prioritization: Console-run -> Docs inline -> Control. Target sample sizes estimated per cohort.
2026-03-10 - Ravi Shah: Blocker noted — console prefill flow requires a small RFC to expand the API key ephemeral token window; created dependency ENG-79210. Added to dependencies list.

risks: Console prefill flow requires infra change (ENG-79210) that may shift timeline
SDK surface differences could make a single quickstart template unsuitable for all languages
Over-instrumentation may increase event costs; need to sample carefully
Regional privacy/regulatory constraints could limit prefilled credentials in APAC
